clue.text: Study indications characteristic in body of water north-west of Iceland

clue.text: Betray 20 in Rome?

explanation.definitionFit: To double-cross someone is to betray them after pretending to be on their side.

clue.text: No problem, mostly, to kick out professional of high rank

explanation.definitionFit: Noble describes someone of high rank by birth, an aristocrat.

clue.text: Suffering US heading for transformation

clue.text: On reflection, I would spot content of fake sport that's not breathtaking?

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the letters run backwards

indicators.note: the contents of a word are its inner letters

explanation.walkthrough: Kabaddi is a South Asian tag game in which the raider must chant 'kabaddi' on a single breath while in enemy territory, so taking a breath is exactly what it forbids.
explanation.definitionFit: Kabaddi is a sport whose raider may not take a breath during a raid, hence 'not breathtaking'.

clue.text: Scruffy final character in Breakfast at Tiffany's eviscerated

with its insides removed, only the outer letters remain

explanation.definitionFit: Tatty means shabby and worn, scruffy.

clue.text: It sprinkles holy water in breathing apparatus, according to initiates

explanation.surface: A strange church ritual performed through a breathing mask for new members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initiates' looks like new church members, fitting the holy-water surface; it is a verb telling you which piece begins the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspergill is the brush or perforated globe a priest uses to sprinkle holy water.

clue.text: Body part seen in northern resort from time to time

explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym by category: the toe is one of the body's parts, the one the solver is steered away from by the seaside surface.

clue.text: Maybe onion is to cry over

parts.note: to blub is to cry, sob

explanation.surface: Chopping an onion makes you weep.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface borrows the tears everybody sheds over an onion, which keeps 'cry over' reading as a single idea.
explanation.definitionFit: An onion is an example of a bulb, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Spits next to hat? It makes me speechless

parts.note: a topper is a top hat

explanation.surface: Someone struck dumb at the sight of spitting beside a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: A gobstopper is a very large, hard, round sweet, big enough to fill the mouth and stop you talking; 'gob' is British slang for mouth as well as for spit.
explanation.definitionFit: With a gobstopper in your mouth you cannot speak.

clue.text: Dribble excitedly over upper-class American singer

indicators.note: the letters jump about into a new order

explanation.surface: Drooling with excitement over a posh American vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' looks like a human star, but in crosswords it is often a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Singer' is crossword shorthand for a songbird, and the bluebird is a songbird native to North America.

clue.text: Delivery from first of youthful employees unwrapped

indicators.note: 'first of' picks out what comes first of the word, its opening letter
the wrapping, the outer letters, is taken off

explanation.surface: Young staff turn up to open a parcel.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a yorker is a ball bowled to land right at the batsman's feet; 'delivery' is the usual cricketing word for a bowled ball, not a parcel.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket sense: every ball bowled is a delivery, and the yorker is one kind, aimed at the batsman's toes.

clue.text: Stretcher produced after basic dental works

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: An ambulance stretcher arriving after some routine dentistry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stretcher' conjures a hospital bed, which the dental surface backs up; read it as 'something that stretches'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic sense: 'stretcher' is read literally as 'thing that stretches' rather than as a carrying bed.

clue.text: Extinguish most of blaze next to small trees

explanation.walkthrough: 'Small trees' reads as saplings, but small only supplies S and trees alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotch firs, better known as Scots pines, are trees.

clue.text: Site Celts developed to produce plums

indicators.note: the letters develop into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Ancient Britons clearing land for an orchard.
explanation.walkthrough: The orchard surface makes plums fruit; they are British slang for testicles.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Plums' is British slang for testicles.

clue.text: Boffin, one enthralled by exotic insect in street?

clue.text: Goodness, one's a yes, at first

clue.text: Disappearance of brightness not good

clue.text: Spirit suppressed by nudist, ill at ease

clue.text: Rise to great height in Persia, somehow

clue.text: Back in Belfast with a north German accent
